questions.q: Which control-plane component is the ONLY one that talks directly to etcd?
options: kube-scheduler
kubelet
kube-apiserver
kube-controller-manager
questions.explain: Every other component, including the scheduler and controller manager, reads and writes cluster state only through the API server. Nothing else touches etcd directly.

questions.q: What is etcd's role in a Kubernetes cluster?
options: It runs the containers for each Pod
It is the distributed key-value store holding all cluster state
It is the command-line tool administrators use
It assigns Pods to nodes
questions.explain: etcd stores the entire cluster's state and desired specs. Losing it without a backup means losing the cluster's state — it is the one component you genuinely cannot afford to lose.

questions.q: A new Deployment needs 3 Pods created, but none exist yet and none are assigned to a node. Which two components act, in order?
options: kubelet, then kube-proxy
kube-controller-manager creates the Pod objects, then kube-scheduler assigns them to nodes
kube-scheduler creates the Pods, then kube-apiserver assigns them to nodes
etcd creates the Pods directly
questions.explain: The controller manager notices the Deployment wants Pods that don't exist and creates the Pod objects; the scheduler then sees unscheduled Pods and assigns each to a node.

questions.q: What does kube-proxy do on a worker node?
options: Pulls container images from the registry
Maintains the network rules that route traffic to the correct Pods
Stores the cluster's desired state
Schedules Pods onto nodes
questions.explain: kube-proxy maintains per-node network rules so traffic sent to a Service actually reaches the right Pods — the mechanism behind Kubernetes Services.

questions.q: What is the relationship between kubelet and the container runtime (e.g. containerd)?
options: They are two names for the exact same software
kubelet tells the container runtime, via the Container Runtime Interface, to actually pull images and run containers
The container runtime schedules Pods onto nodes
kubelet runs only on the control plane, never on worker nodes
questions.explain: kubelet is the per-node agent that receives Pod specs and delegates the actual work of pulling images and running containers to the container runtime through the CRI.
